grh_4c0ada8643f5381953d6.title: Susan Comes Marching Home
paragraphs: Riverâ€™s End welcomes home Army nurse Susan Anderson, who has survived wartime service and years in a Japanese prison camp. Susan has only thirty days of leave before returning to duty, and she has already decided what she wants most: to marry Hillary Dana, the shy lumber-mill owner she has loved since their school days. Hillary loves Susan too, but feels inadequate beside a decorated Army captain and is so painfully bashful that every attempt to propose collapses into comic disaster. grh_4c397f9a59cabe331359.title: Revenge at Harness Creek
paragraphs: After young Lex Harcourt is killed by Adam Robey, Lex's brother, Sheriff Cash Harcourt, becomes determined to settle the matter with vengeance rather than a trial. Robey claims Lex drew first and agrees to surrender only if Britt will deliver him to the district marshal at Standish Falls. Cash catches them on the trail and prepares to kill Robey, but Britt stands unarmed between the two men and makes Cash face the fact that revenge would require murdering a friend as well. grh_4c98187aad631b83885b.title: The Panther
paragraphs: A young frontier woman traveling home through a forest ignores warnings that a large panther has been killing livestock in the area. As darkness closes in and the animal stalks her, she takes refuge in an abandoned house, only to have the panther force its way inside. She retreats upstairs and finally into the attic, dragging a heavy trunk across the trap door while the animal repeatedly hurls itself against the weakening barrier. Just as her strength and the hinges are giving out, help arrives below. More than a century later, her descendant remembers the ordeal whenever he drives past the modern highway interchange built over the site where his great-great-grandmother fought for her life.
